summary.intent: Stop two concurrent addrConn connection attempts (orphaned transports, flaky `Test/AuthorityRevive`) by keeping `ac.mu` held from the Idle check in `connect()` and from `updateAddrs` through the Connecting transition in `resetTransport`, which becomes `resetTransportAndUnlock`.
summary.issue_fit: Met. Issue #7365's root cause (mutex released between the Idle check and the Connecting transition) is closed at both callers; the PR's 100000-run flake measurement was not repeatable here and is treated as a supporting assertion.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff (`clientconn.go`) reviewed with callers in `balancer_wrapper.go`; no test files changed. Reviewer-executed at head: `go vet .` clean; `go test -count=1 -race -run Test/AuthorityRevive ./xds/internal/xdsclient/tests/` passed once (one pass is weak evidence for a 0.4% flake). Three concurrency safety premises were independently verified as holding.

observations.fact: The change adds no deterministic regression test; the only evidence for the race fix is the statistical flake rate of an unrelated xDS test.
observations.evidence: `clientconn.go` is the only file in the merge-base manifest.

tasks.premise: Every return path of resetTransportAndUnlock releases ac.mu exactly once and both callers hand it the held lock without further ac.mu use.
Holding ac.mu across the go handoff in updateAddrs cannot deadlock with the deferred GracefulClose/onClose or updateState.
At most one connection attempt starts per Idle-to-Connecting transition because the Idle check and the Connecting set share one ac.mu critical section.
